fact: ASAPP says it has engaged the SARB on its Banks Act Exemption and Authorisation Framework, covering future authorisation of payment activities for regulated fintech payment providers.

The South African Reserve Bank bought a 50% stake in BankservAfrica in November 2025, renamed PayInc, the automated clearing house for national and pan-African retail, government, banking and corporate transactions, and says it wants PayInc to be a payment utility.

The document says a proposed activity-based authorisation framework for non-banks performing payment activities is still being developed, with the draft in industry engagement and piloting and release expected in the first quarter of 2027 (Standard Bank's Nthabiseng Mohale).

TechCentral reports the South African Reserve Bank took a 50% interest in PayInc, operator of PayShap, in late 2025, and the 2026 budget speech named PayInc the shared digital payments infrastructure supporting interoperability across providers.

The South African Reserve Bank's National Payment System Department says it regulates payment systems, third-party payment providers and e-money providers, with access to the payment system by designation or authorisation under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998 and its directives.
Notice 2024 of 2022 records the SARB revoking the designation of SIRESS and designating the SADC Real Time Gross Settlement System (SADC-RTGS) as a designated settlement system.
The SARB speech says qualifying regional payments are currently carried on SADC-RTGS and are to move to the TCIB system by end-April 2027.

TechCabal reports that the South African Reserve Bank published a May 2026 draft framework for non-bank payment and e-money authorisation, with a final authorisation framework planned by end November 2026 per Governor Kganyago.

The CMA committee's paper of 31 July 2024 says the South African Reserve Bank directed banks to arrange with PASA the wind-down of the interim cross-border EFT solution, as part of the committee's oversight of CMA payment systems.
